topics.topic: Whether to remove the concrete passing test value or reference it through an imported named data-provider constant
questions: The concrete passing value must be removed from the note or supplied through an imported named constant and referenced by that constant's name.
Replace the inline numeric witness with a named imported constant supplied by the data provider, or state the expectation solely relative to the imported OBJECT_FLOOR_AREA_MIN_EXCLUSIVE constant.
Replace the inline one-hundredth value with the name of an imported constant that supplies the test value, or remove this concrete value from the note.
Move the concrete passing value into a data-provider symbol and name that imported symbol and its type instead of exposing the value in the note.

quotes: a floor area of one hundredth passes as given
judgement.why: The note embeds a concrete numeric test value instead of naming an imported data-provider constant or expressing the expectation relative to one.
judgement.rule:
Inline-данные: таблицы соответствий, allow-lists, пороги, TTL, пути, рейтинги, размеры, словари alias'ов. Значение размещается процедурой 15.2 и доходит до кода одним из трёх путей §15.3.1; note называет
  перечисление адресом `= models.SomeStatus` (член — его именем рядом с адресом, §15.3.1),
  константу — именем импортируемого символа
  (`the imported RETRY_LIMIT constant`), настройку — полем объекта настроек.

topics.topic: Whether to permit byte-at-a-time reads or bounded reads past the delimiter
questions: Which requirement must change: allow one-byte reads so the implementation can stop exactly at an arbitrarily aligned delimiter, or allow a read to consume bytes past the delimiter's end while ensuring those bytes are never returned?

Which requirement must change: the absolute prohibition on reading past an as-yet-undetected delimiter, or the requirement to fill the holding buffer in multi-byte pieces? With only the ByteStream read operation, a multi-byte read can contain the delimiter followed by bytes past its end.

Which requirement must change: permitting bounded lookahead past the delimiter, or permitting byte-at-a-time reads when needed to locate the delimiter exactly? With only ByteStream.read(size), multi-byte reads can cross the delimiter when its position is not aligned with a read boundary.

quotes: never reading from stream a byte past the delimiter's end
it MUST hold, read and not yet answered, never more bytes than the delimiter's length, and MUST read the file in pieces that fill that holding, never one byte at a time
judgement.why: With only ByteStream.read(size), locating an arbitrarily aligned delimiter without ever consuming a following byte can require one-byte reads, while the other obligation forbids such reads and requires multi-byte pieces that can cross the delimiter.

topics.topic: Decide whether model_items receives explicit field lists or may enumerate declared Pydantic fields generically
questions: Either the runtime model surface must list every readable field, or model_items must be explicitly permitted to enumerate and read declared Pydantic fields generically.

Either model_items must receive a finite imported model surface whose fields can be addressed directly by name, or the gate must permit a non-probing Pydantic field-enumeration operation for this generic function.
Either list every supported model type and its fields, or explicitly exempt model_items from the listed-field-only rule so it may enumerate declared fields generically.
Either provide the field names so they can be addressed directly, or exempt model_items' generic model-field iteration from the requirement that every field be addressed directly by name.

quotes: model_items: [RETURN_SHAPE] MUST answer, for a value that is a model of the models module, one pair for each field the model declares, holding the field's name and the value the field holds, in the order the model declares its fields, and MUST answer None for any other value, a tuple, an enumeration member and None included.

Reflective attribute access is rejected: never call getattr, hasattr,
  setattr, delattr, or vars; every declared field and operation is
  addressed directly by name, including in try/finally cleanup.
No imported runtime model symbols.
Read from a model value only the fields listed for its type; never use getattr(value, name, default) to probe for a field that is not declared.
judgement.why: The function must return every declared field of every models-module model, but no runtime model fields are listed and the Factory requires every field to be listed and addressed directly by name, so satisfying the return obligation necessarily breaks the field-access obligations.

topics.topic: Define how model_items identifies the supported runtime model types
questions: Either runtime model types must be imported so model_items can identify models owned by the models module, or the requirement must define supported models using the available BaseModel type.

quotes: model_items: [RETURN_SHAPE] MUST answer, for a value that is a model of the models module, one pair for each field the model declares, holding the field's name and the value the field holds, in the order the model declares its fields, and MUST answer None for any other value, a tuple, an enumeration member and None included.
judgement.why: The requirement defines the supported values behaviorally as models of the models module and excludes every other value; the internal identification technique is not a separate observable requirement.

topics.topic: Resolve whether the value parameter may use object when declared by the contract
questions: Either the contract's value parameter type must change from object, or the generation instruction must permit object when the CONTRACTS signature explicitly declares it.

quotes: def model_items(value: object) -> tuple[tuple[str, object], ...] | None
Import from IMPORTS every symbol the module uses, including symbols used only in annotations, and annotate each parameter with the type its CONTRACTS signature declares, never object or nothing.
judgement.why: The contract requires the value parameter to be annotated as object while the generation instruction simultaneously requires contract-declared parameter types and forbids object, so either annotation violates one obligation.

topics.topic: How load_configuration may directly access RuntimeSettings fields identified only by imported string constants
questions: The three imported constants identify RuntimeSettings fields only as runtime strings, while the gate requires every field to be addressed directly and forbids reflective lookup; either replace the string-name constants with a typed/direct access surface, expose their field mapping in the prompt, or permit the required reflective access.

quotes: load_configuration: [VALIDATION_ERROR] MUST check the settings load_runtime_settings answers in this order and answer a StartDiagnostic at the first check that fails, naming the failed check and the failed item by its RuntimeSettings field name, the equal-secrets check both items of the first equal pair in that order, the check that the two ports differ the service_listen item alone, and never a value, items within one check taken in the order of the imported RUNTIME_SETTING_ORDER constant: the items the imported RUNTIME_SETTINGS_ALL_OR_NONE constant names all set or all unset, a partial set failing on its first unset item; each item the imported RUNTIME_SETTINGS_REQUIRED constant names set; each address well formed; the two addresses' ports different; each secret at least the imported SECRET_MIN_BYTES constant in bytes of its text encoded by the imported TEXT_ENCODING constant, a secret whose text cannot be so encoded failing that check for its item, so that no setting makes the check raise; no two secrets equal; the store and the backup location apart.

Reflective attribute access is rejected: never call getattr, hasattr,
  setattr, delattr, or vars; every declared field and operation is
  addressed directly by name, including in try/finally cleanup.

IMPORTED DATA ACCESS SIGNATURES (constants from the imports above — read them, never redefine them; their values are not part of this context):
RUNTIME_SETTINGS_ALL_OR_NONE: tuple[str, ...]
RUNTIME_SETTINGS_REQUIRED: tuple[str, ...]
RUNTIME_SETTING_ORDER: tuple[str, ...]
SECRET_MIN_BYTES: int
TEXT_ENCODING: str
judgement.why: The validation obligation requires selecting RuntimeSettings fields from imported runtime strings whose values are withheld, while the static gate requires those fields to be addressed directly by name and rejects the reflective access needed to resolve such strings.

topics.topic: Whether read_listen_address guarantees an unbracketed host or load_configuration may normalize it
questions: Must read_listen_address's imported contract guarantee that every returned ListenAddress already has its host without brackets, or must load_configuration be allowed to normalize the returned address instead of putting that ListenAddress into LoadedConfiguration unchanged?

quotes: load_configuration: [RETURN_SHAPE] MUST answer, when every check passes, a LoadedConfiguration holding the store path and the backup location as the check of the store and the backup location apart resolved them and each listener address as a ListenAddress of its host without brackets and its port as an integer, the service API's address None for an owner-only start; it MUST keep the checked secrets in the module's memory, from which the give functions answer them, and MUST put no secret into its answer.

load_configuration: [ORCHESTRATION] MUST judge an address item well formed exactly when read_listen_address answers a ListenAddress for its text, and MUST put that ListenAddress into its LoadedConfiguration, parsing no address in any other way.
def read_listen_address(text: str) -> ListenAddress | None
judgement.why: In an admissible history where read_listen_address returns a ListenAddress whose host retains brackets, putting that ListenAddress into LoadedConfiguration violates the unbracketed-host obligation, while replacing or reparsing it to remove brackets violates the obligation to put that ListenAddress into the result and parse no other way.

topics.topic: Define how each STORE_COMPANION_SUFFIXES entry maps to a companion DiscardStep member
questions: Which DiscardStep member corresponds to each suffix in STORE_COMPANION_SUFFIXES? The imported constant contains only suffix strings and may have any tuple length, while failures must use the three fixed companion-step members; change the constant to carry the step with each suffix, provide an imported suffix-to-step mapping, or constrain and specify the correspondence.

STORE_COMPANION_SUFFIXES has the declared type tuple[str, ...], so it may contain any number of suffixes and carries no DiscardStep for each suffix, while every failed companion removal must be represented by one of exactly three companion steps. Which passage must change: must the imported policy carry suffix-to-DiscardStep pairs, or must the requirement constrain and map the suffix tuple to those three enum members?

The imported suffix tuple supplies only strings and may contain any number and order of suffixes, while every failed companion removal must be represented by one of three suffix-specific DiscardStep members; which suffix maps to which member is not available to the generated module. Must STORE_COMPANION_SUFFIXES instead carry the corresponding DiscardStep for each suffix, must a separate imported mapping be provided, or must the note constrain and define the tuple's exact positional correspondence to COMPANION_WAL, COMPANION_SHM and COMPANION_JOURNAL?

quotes: STORE_COMPANION_SUFFIXES: tuple[str, ...]

discard_new_store: [PATH_OR_ARTIFACT_POLICY] MUST act only on a store open_store made new in this process, answering removed false and touching nothing otherwise; it MUST close the store's connection, then remove each companion file whose path is the store's path followed by a suffix of the imported STORE_COMPANION_SUFFIXES constant, in the order of that constant, and last the store's file, reading each path's type without following a link, removing only a regular file, passing over a path that does not exist, and stopping at the first step that fails.

discard_new_store: [RETURN_SHAPE] MUST answer a DiscardResult whose removed is true only when the store's path no longer names a file, and whose failure, for the first step that failed, names its member of = models.DiscardStep and its member of = models.DiscardFailureKind: the CLOSE_FAILED member of = models.DiscardFailureKind for a close that fails, the NOT_REGULAR_FILE member of = models.DiscardFailureKind for a link, directory or other non-regular object, the TYPE_UNREADABLE member of = models.DiscardFailureKind for a type it cannot read, the REMOVE_FAILED member of = models.DiscardFailureKind for a removal that fails; after a failed close it MUST try nothing else.
DiscardStep enum members: CLOSE_CONNECTION='close_connection', COMPANION_JOURNAL='companion_journal', COMPANION_SHM='companion_shm', COMPANION_WAL='companion_wal', STORE_FILE='store_file'
judgement.divergence: One implementer maps companion suffixes positionally to COMPANION_WAL, COMPANION_SHM and COMPANION_JOURNAL, while another assigns those members in a different order or reuses one for additional suffixes; a caller inspecting DiscardResult.failure.step observes different failure identities for the same failed path.
judgement.why: The suffix policy supplies only ordered strings while the required failure result needs a suffix-specific DiscardStep, so the texts leave an externally visible mapping choice open.

topics.topic: Policy for confirmation-binding digest collisions and the differing-input guarantee
questions: Must digest collisions be excluded from admissible histories, or must the retained binding distinguish colliding serialisations so that every changed input is refused?

Must digest collisions be excluded from admissible histories or disambiguated so every changed binding is refused, or must the absolute differing-input guarantee be weakened to permit colliding serialisations to be accepted as equal?

quotes: _confirmation_binding_digest: [DETERMINISM_OR_ORDERING] MUST answer the hexadecimal text of a collision-resistant cryptographic digest of one unambiguous serialisation of the action, then the target, then the version, then every field of inputs in the order its model declares them, lists in the order given and an absent value told apart from an empty one, so that equal arguments always give equal serialisations and so equal digests, and different arguments always different serialisations, two of which share a digest only by a collision of the digest itself, never by the serialisation; walking inputs it MUST take a model's fields, each name with its value in their declared order, and tell a model from any other value only through model_items, and take a tuple's elements in their order.

show_confirmation_step: [BEHAVIOR] MUST replace the session's pending confirmation with a new PendingConfirmation holding a new value from make_secret_value, the given action with its target and with shown_version as its stated version, the digest _confirmation_binding_digest gives for them and inputs, and the monotonic_reading it was shown at, and MUST answer that value; it MUST never keep inputs themselves.

take_confirmation: [BEHAVIOR] MUST, once presented_value equals the pending value, clear the pending confirmation whatever follows, then answer ConfirmationTaken when action, target, stated_version and the digest _confirmation_binding_digest gives for them and inputs all equal the pending ones, and otherwise refuse with the CONFIRMATION_REFUSED member of = models.RefusalCode at the stage the imported REFUSAL_STAGE_AUTHENTICATION constant names and one failure of the CONFIRMATION_BOUND_ELSEWHERE member of = models.RefusalKind with an empty path.
judgement.why: The texts define binding by equality of the retained cryptographic digest, explicitly acknowledge possible digest collisions, forbid retaining the inputs, and therefore specify that colliding distinct serialisations are accepted as equal rather than disambiguated.

topics.topic: Decide whether unknown-project refusal uses a failure containing models.RefusalKind.UNKNOWN_PROJECT or changes ProjectCardReadOutcome to admit RefusalKind directly
questions: Must the test say that read_project_card answers a Refusal carrying a failure with the UNKNOWN_PROJECT member of = models.RefusalKind, or must ProjectCardReadOutcome be changed to admit RefusalKind directly?

quotes: read_project_card: [BEHAVIOR] MUST answer a Refusal with the NOT_FOUND member of = models.RefusalCode at the stage the imported REFUSAL_STAGE_EXISTENCE constant names and one failure of the UNKNOWN_PROJECT member of = models.RefusalKind, its path naming the project_id input, when load_project finds no project, and otherwise ProjectCardFound holding the _project_card of the project whatever its status, an anonymised project answering its erased form and never a refusal; it MUST change nothing.

ProjectCardReadOutcome discriminated union on field 'outcome' (exact variants, no others exist): ProjectCardFound (outcome='accepted'), Refusal (outcome='refused'); a value of ProjectCardReadOutcome is an instance of one of these variants, never of another model, and ProjectCardReadOutcome itself is not constructed
Refusal fields (exact, no others exist): code: RefusalCode, failures: tuple[RefusalFailure, ...], outcome: Literal['refused'], stage: int | None
RefusalFailure fields (exact, no others exist): kind: RefusalKind, path: tuple[PathElement, ...]
judgement.why: The behavior explicitly requires a Refusal whose failures contain an UNKNOWN_PROJECT RefusalFailure, while the closed ProjectCardReadOutcome union admits Refusal but not RefusalKind directly.

topics.topic: Whether the dependency boundary must pass the newly created customer_ref to write_imported_project
questions: Must the dependency boundary permit applying the customer_ref returned by make_imported_customer, or must the orchestration stop requiring that minted value to be passed to write_imported_project?
Must the dependency boundary also allow the customer_ref returned by make_imported_customer, or must the orchestration stop applying that minted value to write_imported_project?

quotes: confirm_import: [ORCHESTRATION] For a clean mapping it MUST have every record written by its own module in transaction: first each MappedCustomer through make_imported_customer with its name, its kind as = models.CustomerKind, its v1 value, its tax-id answer and instant; then each picked project through write_imported_project with the display name and alias it arrives under and the customer_ref minted for its v1 value, or None when it names none; then each brought-in pointer through write_imported_pointer with the file's digest.

confirm_import: [DEPENDENCY_BOUNDARY] MUST leave every write to the record's own module: it MUST NOT write a record itself, MUST NOT open, commit or roll back a transaction, MUST NOT write the migration closure, and MUST NOT apply any value other than those of the kept file of the bound digest, those choices carries and the given instant.
judgement.why: For a picked project naming a customer, the orchestration requires passing the newly minted customer_ref returned by make_imported_customer to write_imported_project, while the dependency boundary forbids applying that value because it comes from neither the kept file, choices, nor the given instant.

topics.topic: How check_store_file must comply with the every-file secure-opening rule
questions: Must the every-file rule exclude the file opening performed internally by check_store_file, or must check_store_file accept an already safely opened file descriptor?

Which requirement must change: must the every-file rule exclude the open performed inside check_store_file, or must check_store_file accept an already securely opened file descriptor instead of only a path?

quotes: _run_backup: [BEHAVIOR] The backup step MUST then read the written backup back from its file, decrypt it with _decrypt_backup into a third new temporary file, have check_store_file check that file against the recorded last sequence number, and remove that file with each companion file whose path is its path followed by a suffix of the imported STORE_COMPANION_SUFFIXES constant, whatever the check answered; the backup MUST be renamed to its kept name only when the snapshot, the encryption, the decryption and the check passed and both unencrypted files were removed, and otherwise the step MUST delete the backup when it can, leaving it under its temporary name when the decrypted file cannot be removed, and report the MAKE_BACKUP member of = models.BackupRunStep, a file it cannot remove or delete staying under the temporary prefix for the next run.
def check_store_file(file_path: str, recorded_sequence: int) -> StoreFileCheck

_run_backup: [PATH_OR_ARTIFACT_POLICY] MUST touch in backup_dir only regular files directly in it whose name begins with the imported BACKUP_KEPT_PREFIX constant or the imported BACKUP_TEMPORARY_PREFIX constant, MUST follow no symbolic link, opening every file through _open_without_link, and enter no directory there, and MUST create each temporary file exclusively under the temporary prefix with a name no other file has; it MUST write nothing to the store and make no audit entry.
judgement.why: The required check must be handed a path and therefore opens the decrypted file inside check_store_file, while the same run is required to open every file through the module-local _open_without_link operation, and the declared callee signature provides no file-descriptor route that can satisfy both obligations.

topics.topic: How copy_store_snapshot must comply with the every-file secure-opening rule
questions: Must the every-file rule exclude files opened internally by copy_store_snapshot, or must copy_store_snapshot expose a file-descriptor operation that can use _open_without_link?

Which requirement must change: must the every-file rule be limited to files opened directly by backups, or must copy_store_snapshot receive an already securely opened file descriptor so its target is opened through _open_without_link?

quotes: _run_backup: [BEHAVIOR] The run's backup step MUST have copy_store_snapshot copy registry_store to a new temporary path, take the key give_backup_key gives, make the BackupRecord from the imported BACKUP_RECORD_VERSION constant, the StoreSnapshot's fixed_at as its made_at and its last_sequence_number, the imported RELEASE_VERSION constant and _key_digest of the key, write _encrypt_backup of the copy's bytes into a second new temporary file, and remove the unencrypted copy, with each companion file whose path is the copy's path followed by a suffix of the imported STORE_COMPANION_SUFFIXES constant, before going on; when copy_store_snapshot answers SnapshotFailed, the step MUST remove what it wrote at that path before it reports.
def copy_store_snapshot(registry_store: RegistryStore, target_path: str) -> SnapshotOutcome

_run_backup: [PATH_OR_ARTIFACT_POLICY] MUST touch in backup_dir only regular files directly in it whose name begins with the imported BACKUP_KEPT_PREFIX constant or the imported BACKUP_TEMPORARY_PREFIX constant, MUST follow no symbolic link, opening every file through _open_without_link, and enter no directory there, and MUST create each temporary file exclusively under the temporary prefix with a name no other file has; it MUST write nothing to the store and make no audit entry.
judgement.why: The required snapshot operation receives a new temporary path and must create or open its target internally, while the run must create every temporary file exclusively and open every file through _open_without_link, and the declared snapshot contract has no securely opened descriptor parameter through which both requirements can be obeyed.

topics.topic: PathElement field exclusivity and serialization behavior for invalid field combinations
questions: Must PathElement guarantee exactly one non-None field, or must serialization define behavior for elements whose fields are both None or both non-None?
Must PathElement guarantee exactly one non-None field, or must serialization define the cases where both fields are None or both are populated?
Must PathElement guarantee exactly one non-None field, or must serialization define how elements with both fields set or both fields None are written?

quotes: _write_service_answer: [RETURN_SHAPE] MUST answer, for a RefusedAnswer, an HttpResponse whose status is the status of the row of the refusal's code in the imported REFUSAL_HTTP_STATUSES constant and whose body is one JSON object encoded by the imported TEXT_ENCODING constant of exactly code, stage and failures: the code's value, the stage as a JSON number or JSON null when it is None, and each failure in its order as an object of its kind's value and its path, a JSON array of its elements, each element written as the one value it holds, its name as a JSON string or else its position as a JSON number, never as an object or JSON null; and for every other variant of = models.OperationAnswer, an HttpResponse whose status is the imported SERVICE_ANSWER_STATUS constant and whose body is one JSON object encoded by the imported TEXT_ENCODING constant of the variant's own fields without answer_kind, each nested model written as an object of its fields without view_kind; for a ValidationAnswer and a ContextAnswer the body MUST be the nested view alone, not wrapped in its field.
- PathElement fields (exact, no others exist): name: str | None, position: int | None
judgement.why: The model surface admits a PathElement with both fields None, but the note requires every element to be written as a non-null value it holds, which is impossible in that admissible case.

topics.topic: PathElement validity versus serializer behavior for missing, conflicting, or negative values
questions: Which passage must change: must PathElement declare that exactly one field is present, that position is non-negative, and that name cannot contain OWNER_FORM_PATH_SEPARATOR, or must _write_form_path define output for None and negative positions and escaping for names containing the separator?

Which passage must change: must PathElement enforce that exactly one of name and a non-negative position is present, or must _write_form_path define behavior for elements with neither value, both values, or a negative position?
Must PathElement be constrained so that a nameless element always has a non-negative position, or must _write_form_path define behavior for a nameless element whose position is None or negative?

quotes: def _write_form_path(path: tuple[PathElement, ...]) -> str
- PathElement fields (exact, no others exist): name: str | None, position: int | None

_write_form_path: [RETURN_SHAPE] MUST answer the text of path's elements in their order with the imported OWNER_FORM_PATH_SEPARATOR constant between each two and nowhere else: an element's name written as it stands and, for an element with no name, its position, a tuple's position counted from zero, written as its decimal digits in ASCII with no sign and no leading zero.
judgement.why: The contract admits every PathElement allowed by the stated fields, including a nameless element with a None or negative position, while the note requires that position to be emitted as unsigned decimal digits, which cannot be obeyed for those admissible values.

topics.topic: Placed policy symbol defining form-path serialization and numeric formatting
questions: This inline numeric-format policy must become a placed value named through one of the permitted §15.3.1 paths, such as an imported provider constant.
Replace the inline serialization grammar with a reference to an imported formatter or other placed policy symbol whose contract defines the encoding.

quotes: _write_form_path: [RETURN_SHAPE] MUST answer the text of path's elements in their order with the imported OWNER_FORM_PATH_SEPARATOR constant between each two and nowhere else: an element's name written as it stands and, for an element with no name, its position, a tuple's position counted from zero, written as its decimal digits in ASCII with no sign and no leading zero.
judgement.why: The note embeds a string-level serialization grammar for positions instead of stating behavior without string micro-syntax.

Нота остаётся требованием к

Replace the inline field-name grammar with a reference to an imported parser or other placed policy symbol whose contract defines the encoding.

quotes: _read_form_path: [RETURN_SHAPE] MUST answer the path a form field's name writes, one PathElement for each of its parts in their order, the text between one occurrence of the imported OWNER_FORM_PATH_SEPARATOR constant and the next being one part: a part made of ASCII decimal digits alone, at least one, as a PathElement whose position is the whole number they name in decimal, a tuple's position counted from zero, and whose name is None, and every other part as one whose name is the part's text unchanged and whose position is None; a text holding no separator MUST answer a path of one element, and the reading MUST NOT raise for any text.
judgement.why: The note embeds the string micro-syntax that classifies and decodes path parts.

микро-синтаксис в ней запрещены.

topics.topic: Imported provider constant for the complete Content-Security-Policy value
questions: Provide the complete Content-Security-Policy header value through an imported provider constant, rather than providing only the header-name constant and requiring the generated module to invent the value.

quotes: _render_owner_page: [SECURITY_BOUNDARY] MUST write every stored or given value into the page as text escaped for the place it stands in, never as markup, telling each value's kind by its declared type and never by probing an attribute with hasattr or getattr, a member of an enumeration of the models module written as its value, and a nested model's fields taken only through model_items and named by the text _write_form_path writes for their path; it MUST give the response a header field the imported OWNER_CONTENT_SECURITY_POLICY_HEADER constant names that forbids every script, and, for a SignedInAnswer alone, one header field the imported OWNER_SET_COOKIE_HEADER constant names whose value is one set-cookie-string, as the HTTP state management standard defines it, whose cookie name is the imported OWNER_SESSION_COOKIE_NAME constant, whose cookie value is the answer's session_id, and whose attributes are exactly those the imported OWNER_SESSION_COOKIE_ATTRIBUTES constant holds, written as they stand, and no other attribute; it MUST NOT write a SignedInAnswer's session_id anywhere in the page, the session travelling in that cookie alone; it MUST never expire or delete a cookie.
judgement.why: Only the CSP header name is placed, so the generated module must invent the unplaced policy value that forbids scripts.
judgement.rule:
- **Fail-closed на обеих сторонах.** Неразмещённое значение останавливает
  сборку. Подстановка значения в контекст модели «на всякий случай»
  запрещена: она молча восстанавливает старое поведение и обесценивает шов.

topics.topic: Whether names may contain the path separator and how such names are serialized
questions: Must PathElement.name be constrained not to contain the imported OWNER_FORM_PATH_SEPARATOR constant, or must the requirement stop demanding both that every name be written unchanged and that the separator occur nowhere except between elements?

quotes: - PathElement fields (exact, no others exist): name: str | None, position: int | None

_write_form_path: [RETURN_SHAPE] MUST answer the text of path's elements in their order with the imported OWNER_FORM_PATH_SEPARATOR constant between each two and nowhere else: an element's name written as it stands and, for an element with no name, its position, a tuple's position counted from zero, written as its decimal digits in ASCII with no sign and no leading zero.
judgement.why: For an admissible PathElement whose name contains OWNER_FORM_PATH_SEPARATOR, writing the name unchanged necessarily places that separator within an element, contradicting the simultaneous requirement that it occur between elements and nowhere else.

topics.topic: Required content and one-line formatting of _stop_start listener-open failure diagnostics
questions: Must diagnostics name no values, or must the listener-open failure diagnostic name the surface and, when present, the DiscardStep and DiscardFailureKind values?

Which must change: must the contract guarantee that diagnostic is one line and names no value, or must the note define behavior for every str, since preserving an arbitrary multiline or value-bearing str unchanged cannot also make it one line naming no value?

quotes: _stop_start: [BEHAVIOR] MUST write diagnostic unchanged, followed by one line end, on the process's standard error, nothing else and no value added to it, a diagnostic being one line naming no value as every step that answers one makes it, and MUST answer a non-zero exit status for the process.

start_instance: [VALIDATION_ERROR] When a listener cannot be opened it MUST close every listener already opened, a close that fails being neither retried nor named, then, only when open_store answered an opened store whose made_new is true, call discard_new_store with the RegistryStore, and MUST end through _stop_start with one diagnostic that names the surface that could not be opened, never its address, and, when the DiscardResult's removed is false, says that the new store was left and, when its failure is not None, the step of = models.DiscardStep and the kind of = models.DiscardFailureKind that failure names; a store this start did not make new MUST be left as it is.
judgement.why: When discarding a newly made store fails, start_instance must pass a diagnostic naming the DiscardStep and DiscardFailureKind values to _stop_start, while _stop_start simultaneously requires that diagnostic to name no value, so both obligations cannot be satisfied in that admissible history.

author_guidance: Before editing, identify the decision's owning state from the phase purpose, question_scope and layer obligations, then choose a disposition for each topic that awaits one.
fixed: repair a decision the owning state must make; do not add later-layer implementation choices merely to close a topic. Record the fix commit and review the changed text once.

carried: name the receiving layer and use --what to preserve the choice, its options and consequences, and the required guarantee every option must keep. Decide any guarantee owned here before carrying its execution onward.
accepted: explain why the remaining choice is permitted. Bring an unresolved product choice to the owner with its options and consequences; absence of a quoted requirement does not decide it.
contradiction and standard_violation take no disposition: repair the offending text in its owning state and review the change. Deterministic transition findings must also close through their checks.
